text: Mainly because it costs nothing. With film cameras every shot had a price, so people chose their moments carefully, whereas now you can take fifty photos of the same sunset. Social media plays a part as well, because many photos are taken to be shared rather than remembered. The irony is that most of them are never looked at again.

questions.question: Why do people take so many photos nowadays?

text: Both have their advantages. Digital photos are easy to store and share, and they don't fade. But people forget that files can disappear too — a broken phone or a lost password can wipe out years of memories. Printed photos feel more personal, and an album is something a family actually sits down and looks at together. Ideally, I'd keep the most important ones in both forms.

text: Yes, I think that should be basic good manners. Someone might be happy with a photo in a private chat but not want their employer or relatives to see it. Children are a special case, because they can't really give permission, and pictures posted today could embarrass them as teenagers. So parents especially should think twice before sharing everything.

questions.question: Should people ask permission before posting photos of others online?

text: I think they do, especially on young people. When every face online has perfect skin, teenagers start to see normal features as flaws. Some countries now require adverts to say when a photo has been retouched, and I think that's a sensible step. It doesn't ban editing, but at least it reminds people that what they're looking at isn't quite real.

questions.question: Do edited photos in advertising and social media have a negative effect?

text: Absolutely. A textbook can tell you that a city was poor after the war, but a photo of children playing among ruins makes you feel it. Photos also record ordinary details that historians might otherwise miss, like what people wore or how shops looked. The only danger is that a single picture can be misleading, so it should be read alongside other sources.
